title: Lead Us with Thy Gentle Sway
description: Lead Us with Thy Gentle Sway in Tonic Solfa to SPANISH HYMN, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 502, “The Pilgrim's Prayer”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SPANISH HYMN; any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lead us with Thy gen-tle sway, As a will-ing child is led; Speed us on our up-ward way, As a pil-grim, Lord, is sped, Who with prayers and helps di-vine Seeks a con-se-cra-ted shrine.

lines: Lead us with Thy gentle sway,
As a willing child is led;
Speed us on our upward way,
As a pilgrim, Lord, is sped,
Who with prayers and helps divine
Lead us, Father! Thou dost know
All the way; but, wanderers, we
And stretch out our hands to Thee;
Guide us, save us, and prepare

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to SPANISH HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
